name: NY-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Goldman lost renomination, but Democrat Brad Lander is well-funded
Republican Jennifer Moore has shown no fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win near certainty
model.rationale: The seat sits in a heavily Democratic Brooklyn-based district, and the Democratic nominee Lander raised $2.4 million while the Republican has no reported fundraising or outside spending. Markets price a Democratic win at 97%, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or funding surge for the Republican nominee would be the only plausible path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dan Goldman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
NY-10 is a heavily Democratic Brooklyn district, and incumbent Dan Goldman lost his renomination, leaving an open seat. City official Brad Lander won the Democratic nomination and enters the general election with a strong financial position, having raised about $2.5 million. Republican Jennifer Moore has no reported fundraising, cash on hand, or outside spending on either side.

With no public polling and no expert ratings, the race rests on the district's +32 Democratic lean and the lopsided resource gap. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97%. The seat remains safely Democratic, with only a remote chance of an upset.
